tasks.title: Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies.

objectives.title: Basic AI/ML Terms
objectives.description: Define basic AI terms (for example, AI, ML, deep learning, neural networks, computer vision, natural language processing [NLP], model, algorithm, training and inferencing, bias, fairness, fit, large language model [LLM], generative AI [GenAI], agentic AI).

objectives.title: AI Paradigm Comparison
objectives.description: Describe the similarities and differences between AI, ML, GenAI, deep learning, and agentic AI.

objectives.title: Types of Inferencing
objectives.description: Describe various types of inferencing (for example, batch, real-time, asynchronous, serverless).

objectives.title: Data Types in AI Models
objectives.description: Describe the different types of data in AI models (for example, labeled and unlabeled, tabular, time-series, image, text, structured and unstructured).

objectives.title: Types of AI/ML Learning
objectives.description: Describe different types of AI/ML learning (for example, supervised learning, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning methods).

tasks.title: Identify practical use cases for AI.

objectives.title: Business Value & Human Assistance
objectives.description: Recognize applications where AI/ML can provide value (for example, assist human decision making, solution scalability, automation).

objectives.title: When AI/ML is Inappropriate
objectives.description: Determine when AI/ML solutions are not appropriate (for example, cost-benefit analyses, situations when a specific outcome is needed instead of a prediction).

objectives.title: ML Technique Selection
objectives.description: Select the appropriate AI/ML techniques for specific use cases (for example, regression, classification, clustering).

objectives.title: Real-World AI Applications
objectives.description: Identify examples of real-world AI applications (for example, computer vision, NLP, speech recognition, recommendation systems, fraud detection, forecasting, knowledge bases, agentic AI).

objectives.title: AWS Managed AI/ML Services
objectives.description: Explain the capabilities of AWS managed AI/ML services (for example, Amazon SageMaker AI, Amazon Transcribe, Amazon Translate, Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Lex, Amazon Polly).

objectives.title: Traditional ML vs Foundation Models
objectives.description: Identify when traditional ML models or foundation models (FMs) are appropriate for a specific use case (for example, based on regulatory concerns, explainability requirements, operational constraints).

objectives.title: AI/ML Pipeline Components
objectives.description: Describe and differentiate components of an AI/ML pipeline.

objectives.title: FM Model Sources
objectives.description: Describe sources of FM models (for example, open source pre-trained models, training custom models).

objectives.title: Production Deployment Methods
objectives.description: Describe methods to use a model in production (for example, managed API service, self-hosted API).

objectives.title: AWS Pipeline Services & Features
objectives.description: Identify relevant AWS services and features for each stage of an AI/ML pipeline (for example, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Q, Amazon QuickSight, SageMaker AI).

objectives.title: MLOps Concepts
objectives.description: Describe fundamental concepts of ML operations (MLOps) (for example, experimentation, repeatable processes, scalable systems, managing technical debt, achieving production readiness, model monitoring, model re-training).

objectives.title: Model & Business Perƒformance Metrics
objectives.description: Describe model performance metrics (for example, accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score) and business metrics (for example, cost per user, development costs, customer feedback, return on investment [ROI]) to evaluate ML models.

tasks.title: Explain the basic concepts of generative AI (GenAI).

objectives.title: Foundational GenAI Concepts
objectives.description: Define foundational GenAI concepts (for example, tokens, chunking, embeddings, vectors, prompt engineering, transformer-based large language models [LLMs], foundation models [FMs], multi-modal models, diffusion models).

objectives.title: GenAI Use Cases
objectives.description: Identify potential use cases for GenAI models (for example, image, video, and audio generation; summarization; AI assistants; translation; code generation; customer service agents; search; recommendation engines).

objectives.title: Foundation Model Lifecycle
objectives.description: Describe the FM lifecycle (for example, data selection, model selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, deployment, feedback).

objectives.title: Token-Based Pricing & Inference Impact
objectives.description: Describe the token-based pricing model and its effect on cost and performance for inference.

objectives.title: Context Engineering in FM Applications
objectives.description: Describe the role of context engineering in FM applications.

objectives.title: Agentic AI & Multi-Agent Concepts
objectives.description: Define foundational agentic AI concepts (for example, multi-agent system patterns for complex AI applications, Model Context Protocol [MCP] and its role in connecting agents to external systems, multi-agent communication patterns, memory management, tool usage, and workflow orchestration).

tasks.title: Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems.

objectives.title: Advantages of GenAI
objectives.description: Describe the advantages of GenAI (for example, adaptability, responsiveness, conversational capabilities, ability to generate content).

objectives.title: Disadvantages & Risks of GenAI
objectives.description: Identify disadvantages of GenAI solutions (for example, hallucinations, interpretability, inaccuracy, nondeterminism).

objectives.title: GenAI Model Selection Factors
objectives.description: Identify factors to consider when selecting GenAI models (for example, model types, performance requirements, capabilities, constraints, compliance, cost, latency, model complexity).

objectives.title: Business Value & ROI Metrics
objectives.description: Determine business value and metrics for GenAI applications (for example, cross-domain performance, ROI, efficiency, conversion rate, average revenue per user, accuracy, customer lifetime value).

tasks.title: Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications.

objectives.title: AWS GenAI Services & Tools
objectives.description: Identify AWS services and features to develop GenAI applications (for example, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker AI, SageMaker JumpStart, Amazon Quick, Kiro, Strands Agents, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore).

objectives.title: Advantages of AWS Managed GenAI Services
objectives.description: Describe the advantages of using AWS GenAI services to build applications (for example, accessibility, lower barrier to entry, efficiency, cost-effectiveness, speed to market, ability to meet business objectives).

objectives.title: AWS Infrastructure Benefits for GenAI
objectives.description: Describe the benefits of AWS infrastructure for GenAI applications (for example, security, compliance, responsibility, safety).

objectives.title: AWS GenAI Cost Tradeoffs
objectives.description: Describe cost tradeoffs of AWS GenAI services (for example, responsiveness, availability, redundancy, performance, regional coverage, token-based pricing, provisioned throughput, custom models).

tasks.title: Describe design considerations for applications that use foundation models (FMs).

objectives.title: FM Selection Criteria
objectives.description: Identify selection criteria to choose FMs (for example, cost, modality, latency, multi-lingual, model size, model complexity, customization, input/output length, prompt caching).

objectives.title: Inference Parameters
objectives.description: Describe the effect of inference parameters on model responses (for example, temperature, input/output length).

objectives.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
objectives.description: Define Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and describe its business applications (for example, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases).

objectives.title: Vector Databases for Embeddings
objectives.description: Identify AWS services that help store embeddings within vector databases (for example, Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Aurora, Amazon Neptune, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL).

objectives.title: FM Customization & Cost Tradeoffs
objectives.description: Explain the cost tradeoffs of various approaches to FM customization (for example, pre-training, fine-tuning, in-context learning, RAG, model distillation).

objectives.title: AI Agents & Business Applications
objectives.description: Define the role of AI agents and describe AI agents' business applications.

objectives.title: Prompt Engineering Constructs
objectives.description: Define the concepts and constructs of prompt engineering (for example, context, instruction, negative prompts).

objectives.title: Prompt Engineering Techniques
objectives.description: Define techniques for prompt engineering (for example, chain-of-thought, zero-shot, single-shot, few-shot, prompt templates).

objectives.title: Prompt Best Practices & Guardrails
objectives.description: Identify and describe the benefits and best practices for prompt engineering (for example, response quality improvement, experimentation, guardrails, discovery, specificity and concision, using multiple comments).

objectives.title: Prompt Engineering Risks
objectives.description: Define potential risks and limitations of prompt engineering (for example, exposure, poisoning, hijacking, jailbreaking).

objectives.title: Prompt Management & Versioning
objectives.description: Describe prompt versioning and management strategies that use Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management.

tasks.title: Describe the training and fine-tuning process for FMs.

objectives.title: Elements of FM Training
objectives.description: Describe the key elements of training an FM (for example, pre-training, fine-tuning, continuous pre-training, distillation).

objectives.title: Fine-Tuning Methods
objectives.description: Define methods for fine-tuning an FM (for example, instruction tuning, adapting models for specific domains, transfer learning, continuous pre-training).

objectives.title: Data Preparation for Fine-Tuning
objectives.description: Describe how to prepare data to fine-tune an FM (for example, data curation, governance, size, labeling, representativeness, reinforcement learning from human feedback [RLHF]).

tasks.title: Describe methods to evaluate FM performance.

objectives.title: FM Performance Evaluation Approaches
objectives.description: Determine approaches to evaluate FM performance (for example, human-in-the-loop evaluation, benchmark datasets, Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation).

objectives.title: FM Assessment Metrics
objectives.description: Identify relevant metrics to assess FM performance (for example, Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation [ROUGE], Bilingual Evaluation Understudy [BLEU], BERTScore, LLM-as-a-judge).

objectives.title: Business Alignment of FMs
objectives.description: Determine whether an FM effectively meets business objectives (for example, productivity, user engagement, task engineering).

objectives.title: Evaluating FM Application Performance
objectives.description: Identify approaches to evaluate the performance of applications built with FM (for example, RAG, agents, workflows).

objectives.title: Business Objective Alignment Metrics
objectives.description: Identify business objective alignment metrics for AI applications (for example, task completion rate, user satisfaction, cost per interaction).

tasks.title: Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible.

objectives.title: Responsible AI Features
objectives.description: Identify features of responsible AI (for example, bias, fairness, inclusivity, robustness, safety, veracity).

objectives.title: Tools for Responsible AI Identification
objectives.description: Explain how to use tools to identify features of responsible AI (for example, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails).

objectives.title: Responsible Model Selection & Sustainability
objectives.description: Define responsible practices to select a model (for example, environmental considerations, sustainability).

objectives.title: Legal Risks of Generative AI
objectives.description: Identify legal risks of working with generative AI (GenAI) (for example, intellectual property infringement claims, biased model outputs, loss of customer trust, end user risk, hallucinations).

objectives.title: Dataset Characteristics for Responsible AI
objectives.description: Identify characteristics of datasets (for example, inclusivity, diversity, curated data sources, balanced datasets).

objectives.title: Effects of Bias and Variance
objectives.description: Describe effects of bias and variance (for example, effects on demographic groups, inaccuracy, overfitting, underfitting).

objectives.title: Bias and Trustworthiness Detection Tools
objectives.description: Describe tools to detect and monitor bias, trustworthiness, and truthfulness (for example, analyzing label quality, human audits, subgroup analysis, Amazon Augmented AI [Amazon A2I]).

tasks.title: Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models.

objectives.title: Transparent vs Non-Transparent Models
objectives.description: Describe the differences between models that are transparent and explainable and models that are not transparent and explainable.

objectives.title: Tools for Model Transparency and Explainability
objectives.description: Describe tools to identify transparent and explainable models (for example, Amazon SageMaker Model Cards, Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluations, open source models, data, licensing).

objectives.title: Safety vs Transparency Tradeoffs
objectives.description: Identify tradeoffs between model safety and transparency (for example, measure interpretability and performance).

objectives.title: Human-Centered Design Principles
objectives.description: Describe principles of human-centered design for explainable AI (for example, user-feedback mechanisms, AI decision transparency).

domains.title: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

tasks.title: Explain methods to secure AI systems.

objectives.title: AWS Services & Features for AI Security
objectives.description: Identify AWS services and features to secure AI systems (for example, IAM roles, policies, and permissions; encryption; Amazon Macie; AWS PrivateLink; AWS shared responsibility model; Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity; Policy in AgentCore; Amazon Bedrock Guardrails).

objectives.title: Source Citation & Data Origins
objectives.description: Describe the concept of source citation and documenting data origins (for example, data lineage, data cataloging, Amazon SageMaker Model Cards).

objectives.title: Secure Data Engineering Best Practices
objectives.description: Describe best practices for secure data engineering (for example, assessing data quality, implementing privacy-enhancing technologies, data access control, data integrity).

objectives.title: Security & Privacy Considerations for AI
objectives.description: Describe security and privacy considerations for AI systems (for example, application security, threat detection, vulnerability management, infrastructure protection, prompt injection, encryption at rest and in transit, data leakage prevention, output filtering and validation, audit trail and logging requirements for AI interactions, toxicity).

objectives.title: Hallucination Detection & Grounding Techniques
objectives.description: Describe hallucination detection methods and grounding techniques to improve output accuracy (for example, Retrieval Augmented Generation [RAG] grounding, output validation, confidence scoring).

tasks.title: Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems.

objectives.title: AWS Governance & Compliance Services
objectives.description: Identify AWS services and features to assist with governance and regulation compliance (for example, AWS Config, Amazon Inspector, AWS Artifact, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Trusted Advisor).

objectives.title: Data Governance Strategies
objectives.description: Describe data governance strategies (for example, data lifecycles, logging, residency, monitoring, observation, retention).

objectives.title: Governance Protocols & Frameworks
objectives.description: Describe processes to follow governance protocols (for example, policies, review cadence, review strategies, governance frameworks such as the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix, transparency standards, team training requirements).
